task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 14, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style newspaper update on the canceled evening stage at the Marrow Quay Lantern Festival, including the implications for ticket holders, vendors and the remaining program.

facts.text: The Marrow Quay Lantern Festival canceled its ticketed evening stage on Friday, Aug. 14, 2026, three weeks before the event.
Free daytime workshops and the lantern walk remain scheduled for Sept. 4-6.
Festival accounts show 2,400 evening tickets sold at a single face price of $25, totaling $60,000 in face-value receipts.
The festival says ticket face values and its booking fees will be refunded automatically to the original payment method.
Refunds are scheduled to begin Aug. 17 and be completed by Aug. 28.
The production contractor's revised stage, lighting and power quote was $112,000, up from a provisional $78,000.
The provisional quote had not been a fixed-price contract, according to festival treasurer Una Vale.
A $40,000 municipal grant is restricted by its award terms to free daytime activities and cannot cover the evening stage under those terms.
The festival has paid $19,000 in nonrefundable planning and artist deposits associated with the canceled stage.
Vale said the board chose cancellation rather than taking a short-term loan it could not repay from current ticket sales.
Twenty-two food vendors booked pitches for the full weekend; nine planned to operate mainly during the evening concerts.
Vendors may cancel without losing their pitch deposits through Aug. 21, but the festival will not reimburse purchased food or travel.
Food-stall owner Ceri Holt has ordered frozen ingredients that can be used at later events, but has already paid for festival signage.
Holt said, "Getting the pitch money back is not the same as getting the whole week of preparation back."
Four musical acts had contracts for the stage; their representatives and the festival are discussing cancellation payments beyond deposits.
Festival director Rian Quell said, "Keeping the free program open is a smaller promise, but it is one we can still make."
The daytime program uses existing indoor rooms and does not require the canceled temporary stage.
The board has not approved an evening replacement event or a date for next year's festival.
The festival began as a school lantern display in 2009 and added paid concerts in 2018.
The accounts supplied do not establish a final festival-wide loss because vendor cancellations and artist settlements remain unresolved.
